target_customer: Consumers who want an automatic private journal of places, people and activities
problem: People forget where they went and who they were with. Fabric automatically logged locations, paths and activities and let friends share moments.
business_model: Free consumer app with no stated revenue model
product_category: Consumer life logging and journal app

founders.name: Arun Vijayvergiya
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch August 2016 says he built the first version of Facebook Timeline at a hackathon and worked on Friendship Pages, Year in Review and On This Day.

founders.name: Nikolay Valtchanov
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch says he worked on Facebook integrations with running and biking apps.

exit.reason: YC lists it as Acquired; no acquirer or date was found. The company was still relaunching its app in July 2018.

competitors.name: Timehop
competitors.what: Resurfaced past social posts and photos on this day

technical_complexity.rationale: A mobile app that logged location and activity passively, with battery and privacy challenges but mostly standard app work.

defensibility.rationale: Personal journal data creates lock in only after long use. Platform companies could copy the idea.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Facebook had On This Day and Google had a location timeline; the Moves tracker was shut by Facebook, which prompted Fabric to import its data in 2018.

market_need_then: TechCrunch described a gap between social memory features and an automatic private life log. No demand figures were found.

branding.domain_note: Used fabric.me, not fabric.com. The name was also shared with Twitter's Fabric developer platform, so searches mix them.
branding.community_and_virality: Launch coverage by TechCrunch, The Next Web and YC's blog, and Product Hunt releases through version 3.0 in July 2018. No merch or fan evidence.

brand_strength.rationale: A generic name shared with other well known Fabric products, with modest launch press and no evidence of a community.

pivots.to: Relaunch positioned as a private Facebook alternative with a timeline and search
pivots.why: Search snippets say the relaunch followed the closure of Moves; the full text was not opened.

outcome_analysis: Fabric launched in August 2016 as a bootstrapped YC startup built by two former Facebook engineers and relaunched in July 2018 as a Facebook alternative. YC lists it as acquired but no buyer, price or date is public, so the outcome cannot be explained from sources. The stalled consumer growth is not documented.
notes: Funding: TechCrunch August 2016 said Fabric was bootstrapped for the time being. CB Insights lists about 120K from YC and a search listing showed a 6M July 2017 seed that could belong to another Fabric, unverified and not recorded. The acquisition is unconfirmed beyond the YC status, so exit date and acquirer are null. The fabric.me site returned HTTP 503 and a Medium post about the new Fabric returned 403. Failure factors uses other because no cause is public. No cause for acquisition found.
